ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.

ElementDescription: Sex of subject at birth
Notes: M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported

ElementDescription: Calculated chlorpromazine equivalent dosages
Notes: CPZ equivalent dosage = (dosage in mg * times taken per day) / CPZ equivalent for drug. CPZ equivalents for drugs were based on both the 2016 and the 2020 publications by Leucht et al. Equivalents were pulled from the 2020 paper unless absent, in which case equivalents were pulled from the 2016 paper.

ElementDescription: Abnormal involuntary movement scale (AIMS) positive or negative score
Notes: Was calculated based on a 14 item scale for people with psychosis. Using Schooler-Kane criteria, positive indicates a score of 2 or higher on 2 or more items, or a score of 3 or higher on 1 or more items.

ElementDescription: Lateralization quotient (LQ) based on self-reported scores by participant on 10 items of the Edinburgh Handedness inventory (EHI)
Notes: Computed by the formula (LQ) = (R - L)/(R + L) where R = total number of responses on the form where the participant indicated they use their right hand (even if they also use their left hand to do that action, i.e. use both hands) and L = total number of responses participant indicated left hand for (including actions participant also uses right hand for, i.e. both hands)
